rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is near relative to what has passed or what is with God; all that is still to come is near, while only the past is distant.
rows.anchor: اقترب للناس حسبهم } بالإضافة إلى ما مضى أو ما عند الله لقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may attach to اقترب or reinforce the possessive construction; the wording develops from people’s account to their account.
rows.anchor: واللام صلة ل { اقترب } أو تأكيد للإضافة وأصله اقترب حساب الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People” means unbelievers, identified by heedlessness about the account and turning away from reflection on it.
rows.anchor: خص الناس بالكفار لتقييدهم بقوله: { وهم فى غفلة } أي في غفلة عن الحساب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both “in heedlessness” and “turning away” are predicates; alternatively, the adverbial phrase is circumstantial with the subject of “turning away.”
rows.anchor: وهما خبران للضمير، ويجوز أن يكون الظرف حالا من المستكن في { معرضون }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Khuzāʿa, who claimed that the angels were God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خزاعة حيث قالوا الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of God’s transcendence disavows the claim that He has a child.
rows.anchor: سبحنه } تنزيه له عن ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are created servants, not offspring; calling them honored servants refutes the claim of divine parentage.
rows.anchor: بل هم عباد من حيث إنهم مخلوقون وليسوا بالأولاد. { مكرمون } وفيه تنبيه على مدحض القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading is reported with a doubled consonant in مكرمون.
rows.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على مدحض القوم، وقرىء بالتشديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: اقترب الوعد الحق } وهو القيامة.

words: فإذا هى شاخصة أبصر الذين كفروا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then suddenly” is the conditional answer; إذا of sudden occurrence can stand for the answer’s fāʾ, while their combination strengthens the link, as at 30:36.
rows.anchor: جواب الشرط و «إذا» للمفاجأة تسد مسد الفاء الجزائية كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the whole situation or be an unspecified pronoun explained by “the eyes.”
rows.anchor: والضمير للقصة أو مبهم يفسره الأبصار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Woe to us” has an understood verb of saying and functions circumstantially with the relative clause.
rows.anchor: مقدر بالقول واقع موقع الحال من الموصول.

words: قد كنا فى غفلة من هذا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They confess that they had not known this promise was true.
rows.anchor: قد كنا فى غفلة من هذا } لم نعلم أنه حق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They acknowledge wronging themselves by neglecting reflection and paying no heed to warnings.
rows.anchor: بل كنا ظلمين } لأنفسنا بالإخلال بالنظر وعدم الاعتداد بالنذر.

words: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipped objects may be idols, or Iblīs and his helpers, since obedience to them makes their followers worshippers in effect.
rows.anchor: يحتمل الأوثان وإبليس وأعوانه لأنهم بطاعتهم لهم في حكم عبدتهم،

words: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله
إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى
rows.speaker: ابن الزبعري
rows.claim: When the Prophet recited the verse, Ibn al-Zibara challenged him that Jews worshipped Ezra, Christians Jesus, and Banū Malīḥ the angels; the Prophet replied they worshipped devils who ordered them to do so, and 21:101 was revealed.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لما تلا الآية على المشركين قال له ابن الزبعري

words: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله
rows.speaker: ابن الزبعري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zibara asked whether the threat concerned only their idols or everyone worshipped besides God; the Prophet answered it covered everyone worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: قال: هذا شيء لآلهتنا خاصة أو لكل من عبد من دون الله فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله
إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the inclusive interpretation, the address applies generally and ما is construed as من or as encompassing it; 21:101 explains the figurative usage or specifies the exception after the general address.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يعم الخطاب ويكون { ما } مؤولا ب { من } أو بما يعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣab is what is thrown into Hell and fuels it, from the verb meaning to throw pebbles; a still-ṣād reading uses the verbal noun adjectivally.
rows.anchor: ما يرمى به إليها وتهيج به من حصبه يحصبه إذا رماه بالحصباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This may be a resumed sentence or an appositive to “fuel of Hell”; the lām replaces ʿalā and marks specification, showing they enter for its sake.
rows.anchor: استئناف أو بدل من { حصب جهنم } واللام معوضة من على للاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubt about resurrection concerns whether it is possible and within divine power.
rows.anchor: من إمكانه وكونه مقدورا، وقرىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading vocalizes البعث with fatḥa like الجلب.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { من البعث } بالتحريك كالجلب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Consider your beginning of creation: it removes doubt about resurrection by demonstrating the first creation.
rows.anchor: أي فانظروا في بدء خلقكم فإنه يزيح ريبكم فإنا خلقناكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation is from dust through Adam, or through foods from which semen forms.
rows.anchor: بخلق آدم منه، أو الأغذية التي يتكون منها المني.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa is semen, named from flowing; ʿalaqa is a clotted piece of blood, and muḍgha a piece of flesh about the amount one chews.
rows.anchor: مني من النطف وهو الصب. { ثم من علقة } قطعة من الدم جامدة. { ثم من مضغة } قطعة من اللحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair may mean formed without flaw versus unformed, complete versus miscarried, or shaped versus not shaped.
rows.anchor: مسواة لا نقص فيها ولا عيب وغير مسواة أو تامة وساقطة أو مصورة وغير مصورة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Staged development displays power and wisdom and shows that what undergoes change and formation once can be formed again; the omitted object signals that these acts disclose more than can be enumerated.
rows.anchor: بهذا التدريج قدرتنا وحكمتنا وأن ما قبل التغير والفساد والتكون مرة قبلها أخرى، وأن من قدر على تغييره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps in the wombs those whom He wills to keep.
rows.anchor: ونقر فى الأرحام ما نشاء } أن نقره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term is the time of birth: at least six months and at most four years.
rows.anchor: هو وقت الوضع وأدناه بعد ستة أشهر وأقصاه أربع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading coordinates “we keep” and “we bring you out” with “to make clear,” expressing the aims of showing power and keeping people until birth, growth, and accountability; yāʾ readings occur in raised and accusative forms, alongside يقر.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ونقره» بالنصب وكذا قوله: { ثم نخرجكم طفلا } عطفا على «نبين»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the form ونقر, the verb can derive from قررت الماء, “I poured the water.”
rows.anchor: وقرئا بالياء رفعا ونصبا ويقر بالياء { ونقر } من قررت الماء إذا صببته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭiflan is circumstantial, construed distributively, generically, or as a word originally used as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: طفلا } حال أجريت على تأويل كل واحد أو للدلالة على الجنس أو لأنه في الأصل مصدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ašudd is full maturity in strength and reason; it is the plural of šidda, analogous to anʿām as the plural of niʿma.
rows.anchor: كمالكم في القوة والعقل جمع شدة كالأنعم جمع نعمة كأنها شدة في الأمور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die when they reach maturity or before; a reading has يتوفاه الله instead of يتوفى.
rows.anchor: عند بلوغ الأشد أو قبله. وقرىء { يتوفى } أو يتوفاه الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most decrepit age is senility and dementia; a reading has a still mīm.
rows.anchor: وهو الهرم والخرف، وقرىء بسكون الميم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At extreme old age a person returns to childhood’s weak intellect and limited understanding, forgetting what he did and denying what he knew.
rows.anchor: ليعود كهيئته الأولى في أوان الطفولية من سخافة العقل وقلة الفهم فينسى ما عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a second proof that resurrection is possible: God brings about contrasting human conditions across the lifespan, and the one able to do that can recreate their like.
rows.anchor: والآية استدلال ثان على إمكان البعث بما يعتري الإنسان في أسنانه من الأمور المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is lifeless and dry; hāmidat derives from a fire becoming ash.
rows.anchor: ميتة يابسة من همدت النار إذا صارت رمادا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rain the earth moves with plants and swells; a reading, وربأت, means that it rises.
rows.anchor: تحركت بالنبات. { وربت } وانتفخت، وقرىء «وربأت» أي ارتفعت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pair means every species, and bahīj is pleasing and beautiful; this is a third proof, repeated because it is evident and observable.
rows.anchor: من كل صنف { بهيج } حسن رائق، وهذه دلالة ثالثة كررها الله تعالى في كتابه

words: يسجد له من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration means subjection to God’s power and decree, or that their lowliness points to the greatness of their governor.
rows.anchor: يتسخر لقدرته ولا يتأتى عن تدبيره، أو يدل بذلته على عظمة مدبره،

words: والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative من may include rational and nonrational beings by grammatical predominance; luminaries and other named things are singled out for fame and apparent unlikelihood of prostrating.
rows.anchor: ومن يجوز أن يعم أولي العقل وغيرهم على التغليب فيكون قوله: { والشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading lightens the doubled consonant in الدواب to avoid gemination or the meeting of two still letters.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { والدواب } بالتخفيف كراهة التضعيف أو الجمع بين الساكنين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be coordinated with preceding terms if one expression can apply in two senses, each predicated of a different subject; specifying “many” distinguishes their special prostration.
rows.anchor: عطف عليها إن جوز إعمال اللفظ الواحد في كل واحد من مفهوميه، وإسناده باعتبار أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a subject with an omitted predicate, understood as “many deserve reward.”
rows.anchor: أو مبتدأ خبره محذوف يدل عليه خبر قسيمه نحو حق له الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an unexpressed verb means that many people prostrate to God in obedience.
rows.anchor: أو فاعل فعل مضمر أي ويسجد له كثير من الناس سجود طاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those for whom punishment is due have earned it through disbelief and refusal to obey.
rows.anchor: وكثير حق عليه العذاب } بكفره وإبائه عن الطاعة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “many” repeats the earlier phrase for emphasis, magnifying those deserving punishment while coordinating them with prostrators in the broad sense.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل «وكثيرا» تكريرا للأول مبالغة في تكثير المحقوقين بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings are reported with ḥāʾ bearing ḍamma, and with حقا plus an understood verb.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { حق } بالضم و «حقا» بإضمار فعله.

words: ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whomever God makes wretched has no one to honor him with felicity; God does what He wills in honoring or humiliating people.
rows.anchor: بالشقاوة { فما له من مكرم } يكرمه بالسعادة، وقرىء بالفتح بمعنى الإكرام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those expelled from their homes are the Muslims driven from Mecca.
rows.anchor: الذين أخرجوا من ديرهم } يعني مكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were expelled without any cause that could make them deserve it.
rows.anchor: بغير حق } بغير موجب استحقوه به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be rhetorically connected, like al-Nābigha’s line denying any fault except swords nicked in battle; another view treats it as disconnected.
rows.anchor: ربنا الله } على طريقة قول النابغة: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view construes the exception as disconnected.
rows.anchor: وقيل منقطع. { ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض } بتسليط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s repelling people through one another means empowering believers over unbelievers.
rows.anchor: بتسليط المؤمنين منهم على الكافرين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without this check, polytheists would prevail over religious communities and destroy their places of worship.
rows.anchor: لخربت باستيلاء المشركين على أهل الملل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads دفاع in place of دفع.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع { دفاع } وقرأ نافع وابن كثير { لهدمت } بالتخفيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read لهدمت with a light rather than doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير { لهدمت } بالتخفيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ are monks’ monasteries, biyaʿ Christian churches, ṣalawāt Jewish synagogues, and masājid Muslim mosques.
rows.anchor: صومع } صوامع الرهبانية. { وبيع } بيع النصارى. { وصلوت } كنائس اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Synagogues are called ṣalawāt because prayer is performed there; alternatively, the word comes from Aramaic ṣalōtā and was Arabized.
rows.anchor: سميت بها لأنها يصلى فيها، وقيل أصلها صلوتا بالعبرانية فعربت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This phrase may describe all four kinds of worship place, or only mosques to give them special distinction.
rows.anchor: صفة للأربع أو لمساجد خصت بها تفضيلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who help God help His religion; the promise was fulfilled when emigrants and helpers overcame Arab chiefs, Persian kings, and Byzantine emperors, inheriting their lands.
rows.anchor: من ينصر دينه، وقد أنجز وعده بأن سلط المهاجرين والأنصار على صناديد العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is strong enough to aid them and mighty, with nothing able to resist Him.
rows.anchor: على نصرهم. { عزيز } لا يمانعه شيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An umma here means a community belonging to a religion.
rows.anchor: لكل أمة } أهل دين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mansak may mean a place of worship, a revealed law or ritual practice, or a festival.
rows.anchor: جعلنا منسكا } متعبدا أو شريعة تعبدوا بها، وقيل عيدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the ones who perform the worship or practice.
rows.anchor: منسكا } متعبدا أو شريعة تعبدوا بها، وقيل عيدا. { هم ناسكوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adherents of other religions should not draw the Prophet into dispute about religion or rites: they are ignorant or obstinate, and his religion is too clear to be disputed.
rows.anchor: فلا ينزعنك } سائر أرباب الملل. { في الأمر } في أمر الدين أو النسائك لأنهم بين جهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet must not attend to their words or let them draw him into debate, since debate benefits truth-seekers whereas they are contentious.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد نهي الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الالتفات إلى قولهم وتمكينهم من المناظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means “do not contend with them,” like lā yuḍārru bika Zayd; this usage is limited to intensive reciprocal verbs.
rows.anchor: أو عن منازعتهم كقولك: لا يضار بك زيد، وهذا إنما يجوز في أفعال المبالغة للتلازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is also said to have been revealed about Khuzāʿa, who asked Muslims why they ate what they killed but not what God killed.
rows.anchor: وقيل نزلت في كفار خزاعة قالوا للمسلمين: ما لكم تأكلون ما قتلتم ولا تأكلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading here exhorts the Prophet and intensifies his firmness in religion, from an expression for overcoming someone in dispute.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { فلا ينزعنك } على تهييج الرسول والمبالغة في تثبيته على دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling to the Lord means calling to His oneness and worship.
rows.anchor: وادع إلى ربك } إلى توحيده وعبادته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight guidance is an even path leading to the truth.
rows.anchor: إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم } طريق إلى الحق سوي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then We made him a drop” means We made his offspring a drop, with the annexed noun omitted; alternatively, We made the extract a drop. The masculine pronoun treats it as a substance, extracted thing, or water.
rows.anchor: ثم جعلنه } ثم جعلنا نسله فحذف المضاف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure resting place is the womb; makīn originally describes the resting place but is applied emphatically to its location.
rows.anchor: مستقر حصين يعني الرحم، وهو في الأصل صفة للمستقر وصف به المحل للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white semen becomes a red clot, then a piece of flesh, then bones made hard.
rows.anchor: بأن أحلنا النطفة البيضاء علقة حمراء. { فخلقنا العلقة مضغة } فصيرناها قطعة لحم. { فخلقنا المضغة عظما } بأن صلبناها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flesh comes from the remainder of the morsel or from what grows onto bones from nourishment reaching them.
rows.anchor: مما بقي من المضغة أو مما أنبتنا عليها مما يصل إليها، واختلاف العواطف لتفاوت الاستحالات

words: فخلقنا المضغة عظاما فكسونا العظام لحما
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjunctions vary because transformations differ; plurals reflect differences in form and hardness.
rows.anchor: واختلاف العواطف لتفاوت الاستحالات والجمع لاختلافها في الهيئة والصلابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read both terms in the singular, using a generic singular in place of the plural; another reading makes one singular and the other plural.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر على التوحيد فيهما اكتفاء باسم الجنس عن الجمع، وقرىء بإفراد أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new creation may be bodily form, spirit, faculties created by breathing the spirit into it, or all together.
rows.anchor: وهو صورة البدن أو الروح أو القوى بنفخه فيه أو المجموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then” marks the great difference between the two stages of creation.
rows.anchor: ثم } لما بين الخلقين من التفاوت، واحتج به أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa used this to argue that one who usurps an egg that hatches in his possession owes the egg, not the chick, because it becomes a different creation.
rows.anchor: واحتج به أبو حنيفة على أن من غصب بيضة أفرخت عنده لزمه ضمان البيضة لا الفرخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s exalted station is manifested in His power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: فتبارك الله } فتعالى شأنه في قدرته وحكمته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Best of creators” means best of estimators; the distinguishing noun is omitted because الخالقين makes it understood.
rows.anchor: المقدرين تقديرا فحذف المميز لدلالة { الخلقين } عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule covers houses you do not inhabit; tenants and people using property on loan may not enter without permission either.
rows.anchor: التي لا تسكنونها فإن الآجر والمعير أيضا لا يدخلان إلا بإذن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking permission may mean seeking information about whether entry is wanted or permitted.
rows.anchor: تستأذنوا من الاستئناس بمعنى الاستعلام من آنس الشيء إذا أبصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, istiʾnās means becoming at ease after the visitor’s unease and fear of refusal are dispelled.
rows.anchor: أو من الاستئناس الذي هو خلاف الاستيحاش فإن المستأذن مستوحش خائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means finding out whether anyone is inside.
rows.anchor: أو تتعرفوا هل ثم إنسان من الإنس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greet the occupants by saying, “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”
rows.anchor: بأن تقولوا السلام عليكم أأدخل.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said to ask permission with the greeting three times; if permission is granted, enter, and otherwise return.
rows.anchor: التسليم أن يقول السلام عليكم أأدخل ثلاث مرات فإن أذن له دخل وإلا رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is better” refers to permission or greeting rather than sudden entry, or is better than pre-Islamic greetings and abrupt entry that could expose a man and wife under one cover.
rows.anchor: أي الاستئذان أو التسليم خير لكم من أن تدخلوا بغتة، أو من تحية الجاهلية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A man asked if he should seek permission to enter his mother’s room when she had no servant but him; the Prophet asked whether he would like to see her naked and told him to ask.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase attaches to an omitted clause such as “this was revealed” or “this was said to you,” intending that you remember and act on what is best.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف أي أنزل عليكم، أو قيل لكم هذا إرادة أن تذكروا وتعملوا بما هو أصلح لكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If no one is there to grant permission, do not enter until authorized: this protects privacy and ordinarily concealed matters, and entering another’s property without leave is forbidden, except emergencies or stopping wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: حتى يأتي من يأذن لكم فإن المانع من الدخول ليس الاطلاع على العورات فقط بل وعلى ما يخفيه الناس عادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If occupants tell you to return, do so without insisting.
rows.anchor: ولا تلحوا. { هو أزكى لكم } الرجوع أطهر لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning is purer because insistence and lingering entail distaste and poor manners, or it is better for religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: الرجوع أطهر لكم عما لا يخلو الإلحاح والوقوف على الباب عنه من الكراهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what you do and leave undone among the commands addressed to you and will recompense you.
rows.anchor: فيعلم ما تأتون وما تذرون مما خوطبتم به فيجازيكم عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uninhabited places include roadside lodgings, shops, inns, and monastic hostels.
rows.anchor: كالربط والحوانيت والخانات والخانقات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means use or enjoyment, such as shelter, storing belongings, or sitting to conduct business.
rows.anchor: استمتاع. { لكم } كالاستكنان من الحر والبرد وإيواء الأمتعة والجلوس للمعاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission for such places is an exception to the preceding rule, which covers inhabited and uninhabited houses.
rows.anchor: وذلك استثناء من الحكم السابق لشموله البيوت المسكونة وغيرها.

words: والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This warns anyone entering with corrupt intent or seeking to look at private parts.
rows.anchor: وعيد لمن دخل مدخلا لفساد أو تطلع على عورات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They make the Prophet an object of ridicule or treat him as someone to be mocked.
rows.anchor: ما يتخذونك إلا موضع هزء أو مهزوءا به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt follows an implied saying; the demonstrative conveys contempt, and presenting God’s sending as assumed intensifies denial and mockery. Otherwise they would say he claims God sent him.
rows.anchor: محكي بعد قول مضمر والإشارة للاستحقار، وإخراج بعث الله رسولا في معرض التسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His intense call to monotheism nearly diverted them from idols by what seemed to be proofs and miracles.
rows.anchor: ليصرفنا عن عبادتها بفرط اجتهاده في الدعاء إلى التوحيد وكثرة ما يوردها مما يسبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They credit steadfast adherence to idol worship for resisting him; lawlā here limits the assertion semantically, not formally.
rows.anchor: ثبتنا عليها واستمسكنا بعبادتها و { لولا } في مثله تقيد الحكم المطلق من حيث المعنى

words: وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat answers their claim that he nearly misled them and warns that God will not neglect them even if He delays punishment.
rows.anchor: كالجواب لقولهم { وإن كادوا ليضلنا } فإنه يفيد نفي ما يلزمه ويكون الموجب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reminder is an admonition or Qur’anic portion; it is from the Merciful because He reveals it, and new because sending is renewed to repeat reminders and vary presentation.
rows.anchor: { محدث } مجدد إنزاله لتكرير التذكير وتنويع التقرير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever a new reminder comes, they turn away afresh and persist in their former state.
rows.anchor: إلا جددوا إعراضا عنه وإصرارا على ما كانوا عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After turning away, they denied the reminder so persistently that they mocked its warnings.
rows.anchor: أي بالذكر بعد إعراضهم وأمعنوا في تكذيبه بحيث أدى بهم إلى الاستهزاء

words: فسيأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزءون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome of what they mocked comes at Badr or the Resurrection; it will show whether it was true or false and deserved belief and honor or denial and contempt.
rows.anchor: أي إذا مسهم عذاب الله يوم بدر أو يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question calls them to look at the earth’s marvels.
rows.anchor: أو لم ينظروا إلى عجائبها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pair is a kind or species; karīm means praiseworthy and beneficial. It may restrict kinds that indicate power or show that every plant benefits people alone or in combination.
rows.anchor: صنف. { كريم } محمود كثير المنفعة، وهو صفة لكل ما يحمد ويرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كل conveys the comprehensiveness of the kinds, while كم conveys their great number.
rows.anchor: كل } لإحاطة الأزواج { وكم } لكثرتها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the growth of all kinds or each kind individually; it is a sign of complete power and wisdom and abundant grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: إن في إنبات تلك الأصناف أو في كل واحد. { لآية } على أن منبتها تام القدرة والحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most were not believers according to God’s knowledge and decree, so even great signs did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: في علم الله وقضائه فلذلك لا ينفعهم أمثال هذه الآيات العظام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty to punish unbelievers and merciful in granting respite, or mighty in punishing unbelief and merciful to repentant believers.
rows.anchor: الغالب القادر على الانتقام من الكفرة. { الرحيم } حيث أمهلهم أو العزيز في انتقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase has an understood “remember,” or is a temporal adjunct governing what follows.
rows.anchor: مقدر باذكر أو ظرف لما بعده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن may substitute for the command ائت, or the command may be governed by an omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: أن ائت } أي { ائت } أو بأن { ائت }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing consisted of unbelief, enslaving the Israelites, and killing their sons.
rows.anchor: بالكفر واستعباد بني إسرائيل. وذبح أولادهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Pharaoh’s people” is an apposition or explanatory substitute; only his people are named because Pharaoh’s role is evident.
rows.anchor: بدل من الأول أو عطف بيان له، ولعل الاقتصار على القوم للعلم بأن فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separate question follows Moses’s mission to warn, expressing amazement at their extreme wrongdoing and audacity.
rows.anchor: استئناف أتبعه إرساله إليهم للإنذار تعجيبا له من إفراطهم في الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tāʾ reading directly addresses and rebukes them; though absent, they are treated as present because the messenger conveys the address, intensifying the call to reflect and fear God.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالتاء على الالتفات إليهم زجرا لهم وغضبا عليهم، وهم وإن كان غيبا حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kasra on the nūn may dispense with the possessive yāʾ, or mean “O people, fear Me,” as in ألا يا اسجدوا.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بكسر النون اكتفاء بها عن ياء الإضافة، ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى ألا يا ناس اتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can hasten punishment yet grants respite so the people or one of their descendants may believe.
rows.anchor: القادر على تعجيل الانتقام. { الرحيم } بالإمهال لكي يؤمنوا هم أو أحد من ذريتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawm is grammatically feminine, as shown by its diminutive قويمة; their denial of Noah was discussed as denial of the messengers.
rows.anchor: ال { قوم } مؤنثة ولذلك تصغر على قويمة وقد مر الكلام في تكذيبهم المرسلين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is called their brother because he belonged to their people.
rows.anchor: أخوهم نوح } لأنه كان منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls them to fear God by abandoning worship of other than Him.
rows.anchor: ألا تتقون } الله فتتركوا عبادة غيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was known among his people as trustworthy.
rows.anchor: مشهور بالأمانة فيكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He commands them to obey him in monotheism and obedience to God.
rows.anchor: فيما آمركم به من التوحيد والطاعة لله سبحانه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah seeks no payment for preaching and counsel; his reward is only with the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: على ما أنا عليه من الدعاء والنصح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah repeats the command: his trustworthiness and lack of desire for payment each separately establish obedience, and together strengthen the case.
rows.anchor: كرره للتأكيد والتنبيه على دلالة كل واحد من أمانته وحسم طمعه على وجوب طاعته

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وحفص
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read أجري with fatḥa on the yāʾ in all five occurrences.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وحفص بفتح الياء في { أجري } في الكلمات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is sent only to warn accountable people of unbelief and sins, whatever their status, so he should not expel the poor to attract the wealthy; alternatively, his duty is clear warning with proof, not expelling the poor to please his audience.
rows.anchor: ما أنا إلا رجل مبعوث لإنذار المكلفين عن الكفر والمعاصي سواء كانوا أعزاء أو أذلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened stoning may mean being insulted or struck with stones.
rows.anchor: من المشتومين أو المضروبين بالحجارة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says his appeal is prompted by their denial of truth, not their threats or contempt for him.
rows.anchor: إظهارا لما يدعو عليهم لأجله وهو تكذيب الحق لا تخويفهم له واستخفافهم عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Open a judgment” means judge between me and them, from fatāḥa.
rows.anchor: فاحكم بيني وبينهم من الفتاحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah asks to be saved from their designs or the consequences of their deeds.
rows.anchor: من قصدهم أو شؤم عملهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark is full or loaded.
rows.anchor: ومن معه في الفلك المشحون } المملوء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drowned those of Noah’s people who remained after saving him.
rows.anchor: بعد إنجائه. { البقين } من قومه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event is a sign that became widespread and was transmitted by mass report.
rows.anchor: في ذلك لآية } شاعت وتواترت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage repeats that God is mighty and merciful.
rows.anchor: كذبت عاد المرسلين } أنثه باعتبار القبيلة وهو في الأصل اسم أبيهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tribe name ʿĀd is feminine because it denotes a tribe, though originally it was their ancestor’s name.
rows.anchor: أنثه باعتبار القبيلة وهو في الأصل اسم أبيهم.

words: إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-fee declarations show that prophets share the mission of calling to truth and obedience that bring reward and avert punishment; despite differences in subsidiary rulings, they reject base worldly motives.
rows.anchor: تصدير القصص بها دلالة على أن البعثة مقصورة على الدعاء إلى معرفة الحق والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rīʿ is any elevated place, related to the word for high ground.
rows.anchor: بكل مكان مرتفع، ومنه ريع الأرض لارتفاعها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The structures were landmarks for travelers.
rows.anchor: { ءاية } علما للمارة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their futile buildings may be vanity since stars guided travelers, pigeon towers, structures for ambushing passers-by, or palaces built for boasting.
rows.anchor: إذ كانوا يهتدون بالنجوم في أسفارهم فلا يحتاجون إليها أو بروج الحمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny that they will be punished for their present way of life.
rows.anchor: وما نحن بمعذبين } على ما نحن عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were destroyed for denying their messenger by a violent cold wind.
rows.anchor: بسبب التكذيب بريح صرصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is a sign; the passage repeats that God is mighty and merciful and that most people did not believe.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك لاية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question either denies they will be left secure with their comforts or reminds them of the favor of enjoying them safely; what follows explains the comforts.
rows.anchor: إنكار لأن يتركوا كذلك أو تذكير للنعمة في تخلية الله إياهم وأسباب تنعمهم آمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens and springs specify the comforts just mentioned.
rows.anchor:
ثم فسره بقوله:
{ في جنت وعيون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palm fruit is delicate because it is tender or because the palm is feminine; alternatively, fruit hangs down or breaks under its abundant load.
rows.anchor: لطيف لين للطف الثمر، أو لأن النخل أنثى وطلع وإناث النخل ألطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular collective نخْل is used because palms excel among garden trees, or because the intended referent is other trees.
rows.anchor: وإفراد ال { نخل } لفضله على سائر أشجار الجنات أو لأن المراد بها غيرها من الأشجار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may mean that, among all who have sex, they alone approach males, or that they approach males among Adam’s many descendants despite more women; “worlds” means sexual partners in the first view and humanity in the second.
rows.anchor: أتأتون من بين من عداكم من العالمين الذكران لا يشارككم فيه غيركم

words: وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created spouses for enjoyment; min is explanatory if “spouses” means women generally, or partitive if it means the lawful part of wives, hinting they also did this with wives.
rows.anchor: للبيان إن أريد به جنس الإناث، أو للتبعيض إن أريد به العضو المباح منهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exceed the bounds of desire beyond people and animals, are excessive sinners, or deserve “aggressors” for this crime.
rows.anchor: متجاوزون عن حد الشهوة حيث زادوا على سائر الناس بل الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten Lot to stop either what he claims or their condemnation and prohibition of their conduct.
rows.anchor: عما تدعيه أو عن نهينا وتقبيح أمرنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten to expel Lot from their midst, likely by driving him out violently and humiliatingly.
rows.anchor: من المنفيين من بين أظهرنا، ولعلهم كانوا يخرجون من أخرجوه على عنف وسوء حال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot intensely hates their conduct and will keep denouncing it by shunning them; this is stronger than “I hate your deed,” which could imply he is counted among them.
rows.anchor: من المبغضين غاية البعض لا أقف عن الإنكار عليه بالإبعاد، وهو أبلغ من أن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot asks to be saved from the consequences and punishment of their conduct.
rows.anchor: أي من شؤمه وعذابه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Lot’s household and followers in religion by taking them out when punishment arrived.
rows.anchor: أهل بيته والمتبعين له على دينه بإخراجهم من بينهم وقت حلول العذاب بهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excluded old woman is Lot’s wife; she sympathized with the people and approved their conduct, so a stone killed her on the road.
rows.anchor: هي امرأة لوط. { في الغبرين } مقدرة في الباقين في العذاب إذ أصابها حجر في الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says she remained among those left in the town because she did not leave with Lot.
rows.anchor: وقيل كائنة فيمن بقي في القرية فإنها لم تخرج مع لوط.

words: فلا تدع مع الله إلها آخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition urges the Prophet to increase sincerity and gently instructs all accountable people.
rows.anchor: تهييج لإزدياد الإخلاص ولطف لسائر المكلفين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warn relatives from nearest outward, since concern for them is most important.
rows.anchor: الأقرب منهم فالأقرب فإن الاهتمام بشأنهم أهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, the Prophet climbed Ṣafā and summoned the clans individually; after they gathered, he asked whether they would believe if horsemen appeared on the mountain’s slope; when they said yes, he warned of severe punishment.
rows.anchor: لو أخبرتكم أن بسفح هذا الجبل خيلا أكنتم مصدقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing is a metaphor for gentleness, drawn from a bird lowering its wing to descend.
rows.anchor: لين جانبك لهم مستعار من خفض الطائر جناحه إذا أراد أن ينحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may be explanatory because “followers” is broader than followers in religion, or partitive for those approaching faith or professing belief only verbally.
rows.anchor: من } للتبيين لأن من اتبع أعم ممن اتبع لدين أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they do not follow you, tell them you disavow what they do or their deeds.
rows.anchor: فإن عصوك } ولم يتبعوك. { فقل إني برىء مما تعملون } بما تعملونه أو من أعمالكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can overpower His enemies and aid His allies, protecting the Prophet from harm by those who disobey him and others.
rows.anchor: الذي يقدر على قهر أعدائه ونصر أوليائه يكفك شر من يعصيك منهم ومن غيرهم.

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read فتوكّل, substituting it as the consequence of the conditional clause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «فتوكل» على الإبدال من جواب الشرط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His standing is for the night vigil prayer.
rows.anchor: الذي يراك حين تقوم } إلى التهجد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may describe the Prophet moving among and observing the devoted worshippers.
rows.anchor: وترددك في تصفح أحوال المجتهدين كما روي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After night prayer ceased to be obligatory, the Prophet reportedly visited Companions’ homes to see their devotion; their homes sounded like buzzing wasps’ nests with remembrance and Qur’an recitation.
rows.anchor: لما نسخ قيام فرض الليل طاف عليه الصلاة والسلام تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means his movements through worshippers while leading them in standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
rows.anchor: أو تصرفك فيما بين المصلين بالقيام والركوع والسجود والقعود إذا أممتهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s awareness of the Prophet’s deserving state follows the promise of power over enemies and support for allies, affirming reliance and reassuring his heart.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله تعالى بعلمه بحاله التي بها يستأهل ولايته بعد وصفه بأن من شأنه قهر أعدائه
